reviews.rationale: Human review decision: serve the owner's-guide body text — 15 minutes of charging gives up to 3 hours of battery life. This is the figure Bose presents as the product statement.

The 2.5-hour figure is the testing footnote's measured condition on the same page (36), not the headline product statement. Kept as CANDIDATE record of the intra-source discrepancy; not to be served as the answer.

FALSE CONFLICT — resolved on review: the two claims describe different trigger events, both true. This one is the connection event: page 28, right after a device connects, the light glows solid blue for 10 seconds. Serve for questions about pairing/connecting.

FALSE CONFLICT — resolved on review: this is the status-check display, not the connection event. Page 37's preamble scopes the whole table: on don/doff (or button press) the status light shows headphone status for 5 seconds; 'Solid blue (5 seconds) = Connected' is what a status check shows on an already-connected headset. Serve for questions about checking status. Both claims approved; the answer system should pick by the user's activity (connecting vs checking).

The only support is the vault manifest's own notes about an uncaptured web page — no source document to verify the quote against. Manifest notes are not an authority. Demoted to gap_bluetooth_version_1: capture the specifications article locally, then re-extract with a verifiable binding.
Human review decision: favor the owner's manual — 30 ft (9 m). The manual is the primary product authority for operating range.

The 33 ft figure comes from Bose's support specifications article (via the curated spec transcription) — an official but secondary source, and almost certainly the same spec rounded to 10 m instead of 9 m. Manual wins per the reviewer's authority ruling. Kept as CANDIDATE record of the cross-document discrepancy.
